title: NFIP flood insurance claim: documents to gather
use_when: Use when a client with a National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) policy is filing a flood claim; for FEMA disaster grants use disaster-fema-individual-assistance, and for SBA disaster home loans use sba-disaster-loan-home.
note: Built from FEMA's NFIP Claims Checklist for Policyholders (January 2026), the FloodSmart page on starting a flood claim, and the Standard Flood Insurance Policy Dwelling Form (44 CFR Part 61, Appendix A(1)) requirements in case of loss. It does not decide coverage, cover private flood or homeowners policies, or cover deadline extensions FEMA may grant after a specific flood.

nfip-checklist.name: FEMA, NFIP Claims Checklist for Policyholders (January 2026; resource page dated May 06, 2026)

floodsmart-claim.name: FEMA FloodSmart, How to start a flood insurance claim (web page; no review date shown)

sfip-dwelling.name: eCFR, 44 CFR Part 61 Appendix A(1), Standard Flood Insurance Policy, Dwelling Form (as amended through 86 FR 48511, Aug. 31, 2021; eCFR version of 2026-11-20)

situations.building-coverage: Does the policy include building coverage?
situations.contents-coverage: Does the policy include contents coverage?
situations.has-mortgage: Is there a mortgage or other lien on the property?
situations.condo-unit: Is the insured property a unit in a condominium building?
situations.discarded-items: Did the client have to throw away damaged items before the adjuster's inspection?
situations.repairs-done: Has the client already paid for cleanup or repairs?
situations.other-insurance: Does any other insurance policy cover the loss?

items.label: Flood insurance policy number and the insurer's name
items.detail: The checklist says to have the policy number, if available, when reporting the claim.

items.label: Policy declarations page showing coverage type (building, contents or both), limits and deductibles
items.detail: The checklist also says to check that the correct mortgage company is listed on the declarations page to avoid payment delays.

items.label: Name of the current mortgage company and anyone else with a lien or claim on the property
items.detail: SFIP Dwelling Form, VII.G.4.g (proof of loss). FloodSmart notes the claim check is written to the policyholder and the mortgage company.

items.label: Current mailing address and phone number if displaced
items.detail: FloodSmart says the adjuster will ask for these.

items.label: Log of all conversations about the claim (date, time, name, what was discussed)
items.detail: Covers the insurer, adjuster, contractors, cleaners and others.

items.label: Photos and videos of all building damage, inside and out, from several angles and distances
items.detail: Include signs of structural damage and the floodwater lines inside and outside the structure. Take them only when it is safe.

items.label: Make, model and serial number of appliances, electronics and items of exceptional value
items.detail: Photos or written notes are both acceptable per the checklist and FloodSmart.

items.label: List of damaged belongings with description, quantity, make, model, serial number, approximate age, value and replacement cost
items.detail: The SFIP also requires an inventory showing quantity, description, actual cash value and amount of loss, with bills, receipts and related documents attached (VII.G.3).

items.label: Photos and videos of damaged belongings that will need to be replaced
Receipts, invoices, bills and other records for the damaged property
items.detail: Checklist: gather supporting documentation such as receipts or invoices, if available. SFIP VII.H.1.c: the insurer may examine books of account, bills, invoices and vouchers, or certified copies if the originals are lost.

items.label: Samples of discarded flooring, carpet, blinds or curtains to show the adjuster
items.detail: Do not discard anything before the adjuster sees it unless it is a health hazard or local law requires disposal.

items.label: Receipts and photos for cleanup and repairs
items.detail: The checklist says to keep receipts and photograph repairs; proof of repair may be requested on a future claim for the same item.

items.label: Specifications of the damaged building and detailed repair estimates
Signed and sworn proof of loss stating the amount claimed
items.detail: SFIP Dwelling Form, VII.G.4: due within 60 days after the loss, even if the adjuster does not provide the form. Includes the date and time of loss, how it happened, the policyholder's interest and others' interests, other insurance, changes in title or occupancy, and who occupied the building and for what purpose.

items.label: Details of any other insurance that may cover the loss
Deed showing ownership and any other property insurance policies, if the insurer asks
Condominium declarations, articles, bylaws and rules, if the insurer asks
